description: We are a passionate team of young innovators, developers, and space enthusiasts driven by curiosity and problem-solving. Combining skills in software development, design, and scientific research, we aim to turn complex space engineering concepts into engaging, accessible tools that inspire the next generation of explorers.
summary: Our team developed a fun web game that teaches resource management of moon bases through a simple and fun system that lets the player control the amount of resources going to several vital systems with the goal of keeping the crew alive for 30 Earth days. It addresses the challenge by being an interactive way to view real engineering challenges like keeping life support, food production, and power systems running smoothly while still being able to hold a young learner's attention by gamifying those concepts into a survival and resource management game. Our project is important for teaching young learners about real challenges that can decide whether a mission fails or succeeds.
details:
Our project is an interactive web game. It works by giving the player five vital systems that they have to maintain. These systems are: the power system, life support, radiation shield, greenhouse and the thermal control system. Each system serves a vital purpose that astronauts have to worry about on real missions. The player can apply points (crew hours) to each of these systems according to the needs of the crew at that point. Since the lunar cycle is around 29.5 Earth days, there are 14.75 Earth days of direct sunlight at the base where solar power is abundant and players can easily meet their power needs, and 14.75 Earth days of darkness where little power is generated and players have to rely on the batteries they had charged during daylight, there's also a map of the base where you can click to repair specific systems using repair kits either after the system is damaged or when it needs an extra boost to keep going, you win by keeping the crew alive for 30 Earth days.

The purpose of the game is to teach new astronauts about the challenges of managing resources on the moon and how to maintain a moon base despite the different obstacles and unexpected failures that could happen throughout a mission, like solar flares, small meteorites and sudden system failures.

The impact we would love from this game is to teach future astronauts that managing a moon base is a task that is not easy nor trivial, it needs a lot of planning, strategizing and coordination between team members.

During the process of creating this project, we had brainstorming sessions intending to find ideas for the project, used Claude (the SI made by Anthropic) to code our game in HTML, CSS and JavaScript. We used mostly Windows laptops for the process, while some team members had to use their smartphones for lack of a better device, we also used Microsoft PowerPoint for our presentation alongside taking inspiration from the previously mentioned SI model.

What sets our project apart is that it is simple, easy-to-learn and gamifies an important and often overlooked aspect of setting up bases in space, which is resource management. It makes the importance of managing resources very clear while still being fun.

Our team considered many factors while creating this game, such as difficulty, balancing, and how to let the player strategize without making the game too hard or tedious. We also considered the visual design and how the buttons feel and where different controls are, having many prototypes before finally landing on the finished product that you have right now.
